name: rootr-cli

tools.name: rootr_list
tools.description: List documents and folders in the connected Rootr (루터) workspace, optionally filtered to a path prefix. Use this first to discover what exists before reading or writing.

path.description: Optional path prefix to filter results, e.g. "/notes"

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config

tools.name: rootr_read
tools.description: Read the full markdown content of a Rootr (루터) document by path (starting with "/") or by node id. Read a document before editing or appending to it so you know its current structure. The response's trailing "etag" line is the current ETag — pass it as ifMatch to rootr_write to guard against clobbering concurrent changes. Note: a successful rootr_edit can reformat the WHOLE document (e.g. normalizing "-" list markers to "*", or table cell spacing), not just the replaced snippet — re-read before another rootr_edit on the same document rather than reusing text copied from an earlier read. A published public URL (rootr.io/p/{slug}) also works: a document of the connected workspace reads normally; one from ANOTHER workspace comes back as its published copy, marked read-only with no etag (it cannot be edited from here), and a password-locked one is refused. Reading a public URL counts as one read against the plan's read limit (Free: 180/day), exactly like reading your own document.

target.description: Document path (e.g. "/notes/todo.md") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_append
tools.description: Append content to a Rootr document, optionally under a given heading. This is a conflict-free, additive operation — it never overwrites existing content, so PREFER this over rootr_write whenever you just need to add new information (log entries, notes, findings) to an existing document.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

content.description: Markdown content to append. To show a LIVE table/spreadsheet/deck/board from this workspace inside the document, put `[[embed:/Path/To/Node]]` (or `[[embed:<node id>]]`) alone on its own line — the editor renders the current rows, not a copy. Paths are converted to ids when saved; an unknown path is rejected with 400. See rootr_embed_node.

underHeading.description: Heading to append under, e.g. "## Notes" or "Notes". If omitted, appends to the end of the document. A missing heading section is created at the document end.

tools.name: rootr_embed_node
tools.description: Put a LIVE view of another node — a database/table, spreadsheet, presentation, whiteboard, form, recording, log store or issue tracker — inside a document, like the editor's "Embed" block (Notion's linked database). The document shows the node's current content, not a copy, so edits to the table appear in the document. Appends at the end of the document, or at the end of a heading's section. Same result as writing `[[embed:/Path/To/Node]]` on its own line with rootr_append/rootr_write.

target.description: Document to embed into — path (starting with "/"), node id, or a full rootr.io URL

node.description: Node to embed: its id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

underHeading.description: Heading to put it under, e.g. "## Data". Omit to add at the end. A missing heading is created at the end.

tools.name: rootr_edit
tools.description: Replace an exact snippet of text ("find") with new text ("replace") inside a Rootr document. Fails with a clear error if the snippet is missing or ambiguous (not unique), so read the document first to copy the exact text to find. Good for precise, targeted edits; use rootr_append instead when you are only adding new content. A successful edit can reformat the WHOLE document as a side effect (list markers and table spacing get normalized), so if you plan another rootr_edit right after this one, rootr_read the document again first instead of reusing text from before this edit. HTML comments (<!-- ... -->) are NOT kept when a document is saved, so do not use one as an insertion marker — the result carries a "warning:" line when that happens; to keep adding at a fixed place use rootr_append with underHeading.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

find.description: Exact existing text to find (must be unique unless replaceAll is set)

replaceAll.description: Replace all occurrences instead of requiring uniqueness

tools.name: rootr_write
tools.description: Replace the ENTIRE content of a Rootr document, or create a new document at a path if it does not exist. This is DESTRUCTIVE — it discards whatever is currently there. Read the document first and pass its etag as ifMatch to avoid clobbering concurrent changes. Prefer rootr_append or rootr_edit for incremental changes. When this creates a new document, the result text includes its address (same idea as: The result includes `url` — the address to open this node at. Use it as-is; never guess or construct it.).

target.description: Document path (starting with "/", created if missing) or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

content.description: Full new markdown content for the document. To show a LIVE table/spreadsheet/deck/board from this workspace inside the document, put `[[embed:/Path/To/Node]]` (or `[[embed:<node id>]]`) alone on its own line — the editor renders the current rows, not a copy. Paths are converted to ids when saved; an unknown path is rejected with 400. See rootr_embed_node.

ifMatch.description: ETag obtained from a previous rootr_read/rootr_write, to guard against overwriting concurrent edits

tools.name: rootr_search
tools.description: Full-text search across the connected Rootr (루터) workspace. Use this to find relevant documents before reading or editing them.

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config

tools.name: rootr_comment_document
tools.description: Add a comment to a Rootr (루터) document (optionally anchored to a block, or as a reply via parentId). DB-ROW-COMMENT — to comment on a **row of a table**, pass the DATABASE as `target` and the ROW id as `blockId`; that is exactly what the row screen does, and the row will show it above its body. Mentioning someone with @[userId] notifies them, and their notification opens that row and highlights this comment. Comments carry a user identity: the comment is attributed to the person who owns the key (account keys and workspace keys both carry an owner). A key with no owner cannot comment. On an "own rows only" table you can only comment on rows you can see — another person's row answers not found. A reply (parentId) always joins its parent's thread: without blockId it inherits the parent's blockId, so a reply to a row comment is that row's comment too.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

blockId.description: Block id to anchor the comment to — or a DATABASE ROW id to comment on that row

parentId.description: Parent comment id, to reply in a thread

tools.name: rootr_list_document_comments
tools.description: List the comment threads on a Rootr (루터) document, optionally filtered to one block. DB-ROW-COMMENT — for the comments on ONE ROW of a table, pass the DATABASE as `target` and the ROW id as `blockId`. Works with any key. On an "own rows only" table you only get the threads of rows you can see (the row author and table managers) — other rows' threads are simply absent.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

blockId.description: Only comments anchored to this block — or a DATABASE ROW id for that row's comments

tools.name: rootr_publish_document
tools.description: Publish a Rootr (루터) document at a public read-only URL (rootr.io/p/{slug}) — outsiders can read it and propose git-style edit suggestions the owner can merge. Publishing is an owner-level action: it needs MANAGE permission, which workspace-scoped keys (including remote-connector tokens) do not carry — use an ACCOUNT key (PAT) of the owner, or ask the user to publish from the share dialog. Safe to call again on an already-published document (republish): the public slug/URL never changes, so links already shared out stay valid — republishing just creates a new published version from the current draft. Returns the slug/URL. Check rootr_document_public_status first; unpublish or change settings via rootr_set_document_public.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_set_document_public
tools.description: Partially update a published Rootr (루터) document's public settings — only the fields you pass are changed, everything else (including slug) is left as-is. Examples: {"isPublic": false} to unpublish; {"allowCommits": true} to let public readers propose edits; {"skin": "tech-dark"} or {"layout": {"cover": true}} to restyle the public page; {"expiresAt": "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z"} to set an auto-close date, or {"expiresAt": null} to clear it. Owner-level action (MANAGE): works with an account key (PAT), not with workspace-scoped/connector tokens.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

isPublic.description: false to unpublish, true to re-enable

allowCommits.description: Whether public readers can propose git-style edit suggestions

expiresAt.description: ISO date to auto-close the public page, or null to clear an existing expiry

password.description: Lock the page so only readers who know the link AND this password can read it (4+ chars); null or "" removes the lock. Team plan and up. Locking also turns search exposure off, and it cannot be turned back on while the page stays locked.

allowClone.description: Whether visitors may copy the page into their own workspace (turn off for quotes/contracts)

allowComments.description: Whether visitors may comment on the public page

noIndex.description: true hides the page from search engines (Team plan and up)

skin.description: Visual skin for the public page

layout.description: Layout options; only the sub-fields you pass are changed

tools.name: rootr_list_document_commits
tools.description: List the git-style change proposals people sent to a published Rootr (루터) document. Shows who proposed what, whether the document moved on since (`stale`) and how many places clash (`conflicts`).

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_merge_document_commit
tools.description: Apply one change proposal to the document. It is a three-way MERGE, not an overwrite: only the proposer's edits land on top of the current text, so anything the owner changed meanwhile survives. If both sides touched the same lines the call is refused with the conflict count — read it, then call again with force: true to take the proposal for those lines. Owner-level action (MANAGE).

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

force.description: Merge even though the same lines clash (proposal wins there)

tools.name: rootr_reject_document_commit
tools.description: Turn down one change proposal. The reason (if given) is delivered to whoever proposed it — a rejection with no explanation reads as being ignored. Owner-level action (MANAGE).

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_document_public_status
tools.description: Whether a Rootr (루터) document is published, and at which public slug/URL. `closed: "PUBLIC_OWN_ROW_PAGE"` (with `isPublic: false` and a `closedReason`) means publishing is switched on but the address is closed right now (the document came from a row of an "own rows only" table) — do NOT hand that URL out; tell the user why and how to reopen it.

target.description: Document path (starting with "/") or node id, or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_duplicate_node
tools.description: Deep-copy a Rootr (루터) node — a document or a whole folder tree — next to the original, or into another workspace the user can access (targetWorkspaceId). Returns the new root node.

target.description: Node path (starting with "/") or node id to copy

targetWorkspaceId.description: Destination workspace id (defaults to same workspace)

tools.name: rootr_move_node
tools.description: Move a Rootr (루터) document or folder to a different folder, and/or rename it. This is the only way to relocate a node that already exists — creating with a target path only works up front. `destination` accepts: a folder id, a folder path ending in "/" (moves into it, keeps the name), a full new path incl. name (moves and renames in one call), or "/" for the workspace root.

target.description: Node path (starting with "/") or node id to move

destination.description: Destination folder id or path — see description for the accepted forms

tools.name: rootr_read_node_access
tools.description: Read a Rootr (루터) node's access settings: its explicit `visibility` (PUBLIC/PRIVATE/null=inherit), the effective value it resolves to, where an inherited value comes from, plus the permission overrides set directly on it and on its ancestor folders. Requires MANAGE on the node — a caller who cannot change access cannot read this either. Call before rootr_set_node_visibility / rootr_grant_node_permission.

target.description: Node path (starting with "/") or node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_set_node_visibility
tools.description: Set a Rootr (루터) node's explicit visibility. PRIVATE hides the node and everything under it from workspace members' role-default access — only the creator, workspace OWNER/ADMIN, and people granted an explicit permission keep it. PUBLIC opens it to the workspace. Pass `visibility: null` to clear the explicit value and inherit from the nearest ancestor folder / workspace default. Existing permission overrides survive, so you cannot lock yourself out. This is the API behind the "공개범위" menu, and it is NOT the same as publishing to the web (that is rootr_set_document_public).

target.description: Node path (starting with "/") or node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

visibility.description: PRIVATE = restrict to the creator/admins/explicit grants, PUBLIC = open to the workspace, null = inherit

tools.name: rootr_grant_node_permission
tools.description: Grant a workspace member (or group) an explicit permission on a Rootr (루터) node and everything under it: READ (open it), WRITE (edit it), or MANAGE (also change its sharing/permissions). Use this together with rootr_set_node_visibility to build "private folder, these three people" — set the folder PRIVATE, then grant each person. Re-granting the same subject just changes their level. The subject must already be a member of this workspace.

target.description: Node path (starting with "/") or node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

subjectId.description: User id (or group id when subjectType is GROUP)

tools.name: rootr_revoke_node_permission
tools.description: Remove an explicit permission override from a Rootr (루터) node. The subject falls back to whatever they would get anyway — which on a PRIVATE node is no access, and on an inherited/PUBLIC node is their normal workspace role. Call rootr_read_node_access first to see which overrides exist.

target.description: Node path (starting with "/") or node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

subjectId.description: User id (or group id when subjectType is GROUP)

tools.name: rootr_list_templates
tools.description: List the templates available in a Rootr (루터) workspace — builtins plus anything this workspace saved. Each has an id, name, emoji, description and `kind` (document | database | tree). **Call this before building a document or table from scratch**: if a fitting template exists, rootr_apply_template gives the team their own agreed format instead of a shape you invented.

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config if omitted

tools.name: rootr_apply_template
tools.description: Instantiate a Rootr (루터) template — creates the real node(s) it describes and returns the created node. A `document` template makes one document, `database` makes a table with its columns and views already set, `tree` makes a whole folder/document/table structure. Get ids from rootr_list_templates.

parentId.description: Parent folder id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL; workspace root if omitted

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config if omitted

tools.name: rootr_save_as_template
tools.description: Turn something into a reusable Rootr (루터) template. Either pass `nodeId` to capture an existing document/table/folder as-is, or pass `kind` + `spec` to define one inline. Use this when the user says "make this the standard format" or asks for a new form/양식. NOTE: a template is workspace-wide and readable by every member — do not capture a restricted node unless the user means to share its content with the whole workspace.

nodeId.description: Capture this existing node, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL. Omit when passing kind+spec instead.

spec.description: Inline definition body, matching `kind`. Ignored when nodeId is given.

emoji.description: Emoji shown in the template gallery

description.description: One line on when to use it

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config if omitted

tools.name: rootr_update_template
tools.description: Change a Rootr (루터) template — its name, emoji, description or `spec`. Editing a builtin transparently creates a workspace copy, so the builtin itself is never damaged. Use this for "change the standard format" requests instead of saving a second near-identical template.

spec.description: Replacement body, matching the template kind

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config if omitted

tools.name: rootr_use_workspace
tools.description: Switch which Rootr (루터) workspace every later tool call works on, by id OR by name — no reconfiguration, no restart. With an account key (PAT) you can switch to any workspace you belong to; if separate workspace keys are configured, the one that covers the target is selected and remembered automatically. Call rootr_workspaces first if you need to see what is available. If the server was started with the ROOTR_WORKSPACE env var, the switch lasts until the server restarts (the reply says so) — after a restart/reconnect, check rootr_workspaces again. (A hosted/remote connector is bound to a single workspace at consent time and cannot switch.)

workspace.description: Workspace id, its name (case-insensitive), or a rootr.io URL to a page in it

tools.name: rootr_workspaces
tools.description: List the Rootr (루터) workspaces the current API key can see. Works with either key type: with an account key (PAT) this lists all workspaces you belong to; a workspace key only sees the workspace it's scoped to. Use this to find a workspace id before calling other workspace-scoped tools, then switch to one with rootr_use_workspace (no reconfiguration needed).

tools.name: rootr_scaffold_plan
tools.description: ALWAYS call this first. There are NO templates and NO domain skeletons behind it — deliberately. It does not classify your intent and it will not hand you a structure; what comes back is the METHOD: `analyzeFirst` (the questions to answer about how this job actually runs before you design anything — the daily and weekly rhythm, what piles up, what moves through stages, what arrives from outside, where money is added up, what causes trouble when it is late, and above all what is UNIQUE to this job), `designRules` (how to turn those answers into structure — nouns that pile up become DATABASEs, "one A has many B" becomes a relation, stages become select + board, dates become calendar, outside input becomes FORM + collectInto, calculation becomes SPREADSHEET, counting becomes rollup), `buildingBlocks` (what the product actually offers), `questionPolicy` (ask the user 3-10 questions — you WRITE them, none are provided), and `loop` (the whole sequence). Design it from scratch every time: a bakery, a dental clinic and an SRE team need different things, and no catalogue of skeletons could hold them. Treat it exactly like a coding request. When someone says "build me this" you ask a few clarifying questions, write the code, compile it, run the tests, leave a README, and report. Same sequence here: analyzeFirst = understanding the requirement · questionPolicy = the questions you ask · designRules = writing the code · rootr_scaffold_review = compiling (fix what it flags, compile again) · rootr_scaffold_apply = building · the how-to-use manual = the README · rootr_test_workspace = running the tests. The user should only ever have to type that one sentence — ask your questions, take their answers, and finish the whole thing in this conversation. If they do not answer or say "just do it", assume the most plausible answers, build it anyway, and record the assumptions in the manual.

intent.description: Natural-language description of what the workspace/tree should be for

tools.name: rootr_create_workspace
tools.description: Create an entirely new Rootr (루터) workspace pre-populated with the given document tree. REQUIRES an account key (PAT) with the workspaces:create scope — a workspace-scoped key cannot do this. PRECONDITION: rootr_scaffold_plan first, ask the user its 3-10 clarifying questions, design the tree from their answers, then run rootr_scaffold_review and fix everything it flags at `error` level. The response carries the same `review` back, so a low score here means you shipped something thin. Build a real tool, not a pile of thin markdown files: mix DATABASE (board/timeline views, seed rows), SPREADSHEET (formulas), FORM, ISSUE_TRACKER and rich multi-section DOCUMENTs where they fit, and set an emoji `icon` on folders/databases/key documents. The `tree` shape follows the scaffold schema in llms.txt (max 200 nodes). AFTER creating: if your runtime can receive HTTP callbacks, offer the user to register a webhook on the new tree (rootr_create_webhook with scopeNodeId) so changes flow back to you — skip your own actorId to avoid self-triggering.

tree.description: Scaffold tree — an ARRAY of node objects to populate the new workspace with (see llms.txt tree schema) Any node may also carry `visibility: "PRIVATE"` (only its creator, workspace admins, and people listed in `access` can see it and everything under it) plus `access: [{ subjectId: "<userId>", level: "READ"|"WRITE"|"MANAGE" }]` — that pair is how "make a folder these three people can see" happens in one call instead of leaving the locking to the user afterwards. A DATABASE node may also carry `database.permissions` (칸/행 lock) and `database.notifications` (who to notify on row changes). A database property may carry `searchExcluded: true` (values stay out of the search index behind ask / AI explore / similar rows — not a read permission) and a `type: "vector"` property needs `dimensions` (an embedding column agents fill with rootr_set_row_vectors). A phone/email/name property may carry `dedupe: true` (warn when the same person is entered again) with `dedupeShow: ["상태","메모","통화 기록"]` (fields of the existing row the warning shows — a relation shows its latest 5 rows) and `dedupeCarry: { label: "재등록", auto: true, exclude: ["접수일"], mark: { "재등록 여부": true, "구분": { map: { "A": "A(재등록)" }, else: "재등록" } } }` (same entry came back: copy the earlier row into the new one — see rootr_update_column); any property may carry `validate: { kind: "pattern"|"range"|"date"|"birthdate", pattern?, flags?, negate?, min?, max?, message? }` (flags a wrong value on every new write, never blocks); a relation property may carry `relationFilter: [{ propId, op: "is"|"is_not_empty", values? }]` (which linked rows may be picked). The title property may carry `identifyProps: [{ propId: "연락처", mask: "last4" }, { propId: "지원일" }]` (shown next to the name wherever another table picks these rows, so same-name people can be told apart). A board view config may carry `cardProps: ["면접예정일","연락처"]` (fields on each card, rollups too) and any view `rowColors` (`[{ propId, op: "is"|"is_not_empty", values?, color }]`). Any property may carry `align: "left"|"center"|"right"` and `wrap: true`; a date property `highlightOverdue: true` (past dates red — off by default), `allowTime: false` (no time) and `allowRange: false` (no end date). A table view config may carry `density: "compact"` and `frozenColumns: 1` (first N visible columns fixed while scrolling sideways). A DOCUMENT's `content` may embed a live table/sheet/deck with a line `[[embed:<name of a node in this same tree>]]` or `[[embed:/absolute/path]]` — it is linked to the real node after the whole tree is built (an unknown name rolls the whole tree back).

mode.description: Lower the review bar when the system-building rules do not apply: "docs" for a document-only tree with no tables at all, "minimal" for a small personal/few-person tree (e.g. a couple's shared ledger) where relations, a how-to-use guide, forms, and rollups are overkill. Omit for normal multi-table workspaces.

tools.name: rootr_delete_workspace
tools.description: Permanently delete a Rootr (루터) workspace. Intended for cleaning up EMPTY leftovers from a scaffold run that failed halfway — the free plan allows only a handful of workspaces, so abandoned shells block the user from trying again. Requires OWNER on that workspace, and you must pass `confirmName` exactly matching the workspace name (call rootr_workspaces first to read it). THIS CANNOT BE UNDONE: everything inside is removed. Never call this on a workspace that holds the user's real work — if you did not create it in this session, ask the user first.

workspaceId.description: Id of the workspace to delete

confirmName.description: The workspace name, typed again exactly — the server rejects the call if it does not match

tools.name: rootr_scaffold_review
tools.description: Step 3 of scaffolding (plan → ask → design → REVIEW → fix → apply). Give it the tree you designed and it returns { score 0-100, counts, findings[], summary } — every finding is a concrete defect with the node path, e.g. a table whose only column is the title (that is a list, not a table), a lifecycle column with no board view, a date column with no calendar, a form with nowhere to collect answers, tables that are never related to each other, an empty guide document. Fix what it flags and review again — like re-running a compiler — until nothing at `error` level is left. The rules are domain-agnostic, so this works for a bakery or a dental clinic exactly as well as for a SaaS team. Creates nothing and needs no workspace, so run it as many times as you like before committing.

tools.name: rootr_review_workspace
tools.description: Step 5, after building. `rootr_scaffold_review` grades the tree you DESIGNED; this grades what really exists in the workspace right now — whatever tools made it. Run it after every build: a design can score 100 and still land broken (a form whose answers go nowhere, a view whose filter vanished, rows that never got linked). Returns the same { score, counts, findings[], summary }. Pass `rootPath` to grade only the subtree you just added, otherwise an older workspace drags the score down and the number stops meaning anything. Fix what it flags with the normal tools (add rows, write the guide document, add the missing columns/views) and run it again until it is clean.

rootPath.description: Grade only this subtree, e.g. "/동네 빵집 운영"

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config

mode.description: Same meaning as on rootr_scaffold_review: "docs" for a document-only subtree, "minimal" for a small personal/few-person subtree where relations/guide/forms/rollups are overkill.

tools.name: rootr_test_workspace
tools.description: The last step, and the one that catches what the two review tools cannot. `rootr_scaffold_review` grades the tree you designed; `rootr_review_workspace` grades the shape of what got built; this one **exercises it**: does every relation point at a row that really exists, do rollups and formulas produce a value on real rows, do board/calendar/filter views reference columns that exist, can the form actually deposit an answer (target table alive AND every question name matching a column — a mismatch makes answers vanish with no error), are sheet formulas computed and free of #REF!/#DIV/0!. Returns { ran, passed, failed, warned, checks[] }. It writes nothing, so run it as often as you like. A workspace can score 100 on both reviews and still fail here — that is exactly the case this exists for. Pass `rootPath` to test only the subtree you just built. Fix every `fail` and run it again.

rootPath.description: Test only this subtree, e.g. "/동네 빵집 운영"

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config

tools.name: rootr_scaffold_apply
tools.description: Create the given document tree inside an existing Rootr (루터) workspace, optionally rooted under an existing path. Works with a workspace key (docs:write scope). PRECONDITION: rootr_scaffold_plan first, ask its 3-10 clarifying questions, design from the answers, then rootr_scaffold_review and fix every `error` finding (same quality bar as rootr_create_workspace — real building blocks with icons/views/seed rows, not thin markdown). The response carries the `review` back so you can see what stayed weak, and AFTER it lands run rootr_review_workspace (rootPath = your new subtree) — that one grades what really exists. AFTER creating: if your runtime can receive HTTP callbacks, offer a webhook on the new subtree (rootr_create_webhook with scopeNodeId) so changes flow back to you — skip your own actorId.

tree.description: Scaffold tree — an ARRAY of node objects to create (see llms.txt tree schema) Any node may also carry `visibility: "PRIVATE"` (only its creator, workspace admins, and people listed in `access` can see it and everything under it) plus `access: [{ subjectId: "<userId>", level: "READ"|"WRITE"|"MANAGE" }]` — that pair is how "make a folder these three people can see" happens in one call instead of leaving the locking to the user afterwards. A DATABASE node may also carry `database.permissions` (칸/행 lock) and `database.notifications` (who to notify on row changes). A database property may carry `searchExcluded: true` (values stay out of the search index behind ask / AI explore / similar rows — not a read permission) and a `type: "vector"` property needs `dimensions` (an embedding column agents fill with rootr_set_row_vectors). A phone/email/name property may carry `dedupe: true` (warn when the same person is entered again) with `dedupeShow: ["상태","메모","통화 기록"]` (fields of the existing row the warning shows — a relation shows its latest 5 rows) and `dedupeCarry: { label: "재등록", auto: true, exclude: ["접수일"], mark: { "재등록 여부": true, "구분": { map: { "A": "A(재등록)" }, else: "재등록" } } }` (same entry came back: copy the earlier row into the new one — see rootr_update_column); any property may carry `validate: { kind: "pattern"|"range"|"date"|"birthdate", pattern?, flags?, negate?, min?, max?, message? }` (flags a wrong value on every new write, never blocks); a relation property may carry `relationFilter: [{ propId, op: "is"|"is_not_empty", values? }]` (which linked rows may be picked). The title property may carry `identifyProps: [{ propId: "연락처", mask: "last4" }, { propId: "지원일" }]` (shown next to the name wherever another table picks these rows, so same-name people can be told apart). A board view config may carry `cardProps: ["면접예정일","연락처"]` (fields on each card, rollups too) and any view `rowColors` (`[{ propId, op: "is"|"is_not_empty", values?, color }]`). Any property may carry `align: "left"|"center"|"right"` and `wrap: true`; a date property `highlightOverdue: true` (past dates red — off by default), `allowTime: false` (no time) and `allowRange: false` (no end date). A table view config may carry `density: "compact"` and `frozenColumns: 1` (first N visible columns fixed while scrolling sideways). A DOCUMENT's `content` may embed a live table/sheet/deck with a line `[[embed:<name of a node in this same tree>]]` or `[[embed:/absolute/path]]` — it is linked to the real node after the whole tree is built (an unknown name rolls the whole tree back).

mode.description: Lower the review bar when the system-building rules do not apply: "docs" for a document-only tree with no tables at all, "minimal" for a small personal/few-person tree (e.g. a couple's shared ledger) where relations, a how-to-use guide, forms, and rollups are overkill. Omit for normal multi-table workspaces.

Good for root-cause-analysis style questions ("why did X happen", "what changed before Y") that need to reason across linked documents and LOG anomalies rather than a single document. tools.name: rootr_create_issue_tracker

Use it as-is; never guess or construct it.

tools.name: rootr_list_issues
tools.description: List issues in a Rootr (루터) issue tracker, optionally filtered by state (OPEN/CLOSED/ALL), label id, type id, or a text query. Use rootr_get_issue for full details of one issue.

trackerId.description: Issue tracker node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

type.description: Issue type id to filter by

tools.name: rootr_create_issue
tools.description: Create a new issue in a Rootr (루터) issue tracker. labels is an array of label ids, type is a type id (both from the tracker's custom type/label definitions — see rootr_read on the tracker or its metadata). parentIssueId nests this issue under another issue (sub-issue).

trackerId.description: Issue tracker node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_get_issue
tools.description: Fetch full details of a single Rootr (루터) issue by id.

tools.name: rootr_update_issue
tools.description: Update arbitrary fields of a Rootr (루터) issue. To close an issue, set state to "CLOSED" and stateReason to one of completed | not_planned | duplicate.

tools.name: rootr_comment_issue
tools.description: Add a comment to a Rootr (루터) issue within its tracker. Comments carry a user identity: the comment is posted as the person the ROOTR_API_KEY belongs to. Both an account key (PAT) and a workspace key work, since a workspace key is bound to the member who minted it.

trackerId.description: Issue tracker node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL

tools.name: rootr_create_database
tools.description: Create a DATABASE node — a typed table with columns, views and rows — in ONE call, optionally seeded with its first rows. **Use this whenever you need a table**: moving a Notion database over, building a kanban board, a task/requirement/risk tracker, anything with trackable rows. Do NOT fake a table with a markdown document, and do NOT create an empty database and then add columns one by one — `properties` order IS the column order, so one call keeps the columns in exactly the order you list them. The FIRST property must be type "title" (the row label). Other types: text | number | select | multi_select | status | date | checkbox | url | email | phone | person | files | relation | formula | rollup | created_time | last_edited_time | created_by | last_edited_by | unique_id | vector. select/multi_select/status take options:[{name,color,group?}] (group ∈ todo|in_progress|done, status only); relation takes relationDatabaseId; formula takes formula ("{수량} * {단가}"); rollup takes rollup:{relation,property?,function}; unique_id takes prefix ("TASK" → "TASK-42"); vector takes dimensions (the length of the embeddings you will store with rootr_set_row_vectors). The last seven types are filled in by the server and take no row value. Views default to a single table view; view types are table | board | gallery | calendar | timeline | list — a "board" view needs config.groupBy (a select/status property id), a "timeline"/"calendar" view needs config.dateProp. Row `values` are keyed by column NAME (or id); date values are { start: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm" or "YYYY-MM-DD", end? }, multi_select is string[], relation is an array of row ids. COST NOTE: by default, every row added to this table (now or later) queues that table for graph extraction (embeddings + LLM) — fine for a handful of rows, expensive for a bulk-loaded roster/log table. Pass graphSync:false for tables you are about to bulk-load; flip it back with `rootr_update_node({ graphSyncOff: true|false })` any time after. The result includes `url` — the address to open this node at. Use it as-is; never guess or construct it.

parentId.description: Parent folder id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL; workspace root if omitted

path.description: Full path incl. name — wins over parentId+name, e.g. "/팀/업무 목록"

type.description: Column type; the FIRST property must be "title"

dimensions.description: vector only: the length of every vector you will store, e.g. 1536 or 3072

relationDatabaseId.description: relation only: the table this column points at

where.description: Filter the LINKED rows before aggregating, e.g. [{ property: "결과", op: "is", value: "부재" }]

properties.description: Columns IN DISPLAY ORDER. Defaults to a single title column named "Name".

views.description: Views, e.g. [{ name: "보드", type: "board", config: { groupBy: "<select property id>" } }]

rowPageType.description: ROW-PAGE-TYPE — the DEFAULT kind of detail page a new row opens as. "SIGNED" makes rows 서명문서/연구노트 (freezes on submit, ordered signatures + RFC 3161 timestamps, undeletable) — 실험 기록 · 점검 대장 · 결재 대장. "RECORDING" makes each row a meeting with audio + transcript, "SPREADSHEET" a per-row calculation sheet, "FORM" a per-row intake. Default "DOCUMENT". This is only the default — a single row can be made something else with rootr_create_row_page.

graphSync.description: Default true. Set to false for tables you will bulk-load (rosters, logs, imports) — otherwise every row added queues this table for graph extraction (embeddings + LLM), one job per row. Flip it later with rootr_update_node({ graphSyncOff: true|false }).

workspace.description: Workspace id; defaults to ROOTR_WORKSPACE/config if omitted

tools.name: rootr_create_view
tools.description: Add ONE more view (table / board / gallery / calendar / timeline) to a Rootr (루터) DATABASE that already exists. Until now views could only be set when the table was CREATED, so a Notion table with four views could only be migrated with one. Existing views are untouched — the server merges, unlike a full PATCH which replaces the whole views array and silently drops anything you leave out. A board needs `groupBy` (a select column); calendar/timeline need `dateProp`. Columns may be given by NAME or id.

tools.name: rootr_read_database

includeBody.description: true → also return each row's detail body (the note under a card). Off by default.

Searches the WHOLE table by title: exact name → names starting with q → names containing q → the identify columns (e.g. last 4 phone digits "5678"); newest rows first within each rank. Returns `{ rows: [{ id, title, subtitle }], total, hasMore }` only — `subtitle` comes from the title column's identifyProps (rootr_update_column) such as "***-5678 · 2026-10-02", so people with the same name can be told apart. Pass the relation column's relationFilter as `filters` to see only linkable rows, or `ids` to label rows you already have. Matching ignores spaces/case/brackets/punctuation and treats ㈜ as (주).

A select value is the OPTION NAME. Call rootr_read_database first to learn the columns. Optionally set `position` to insert at an index. Pass `body` to also write the row's DETAIL PAGE (the note shown under a kanban card's properties) — that page is created on demand, so a row with `body` is the one-call equivalent of "메모 추가".

databaseId.description: DATABASE node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL (e.g. "/제작 공정/칸반")

To MOVE a kanban card to another column, set its select/status property to the new option name. Optionally set `position` to reorder the row.

databaseId.description: DATABASE node id, or its path starting with "/", or a full rootr.io URL (e.g. "/제작 공정/칸반")

rowId.description: Row id (must belong to the database)

body.description: The row's detail body — the note shown under a kanban card's properties, in markdown (행의 상세 내용/본문 메모). Creates the row's page on demand; replaces the whole body.

tools.name: rootr_bulk_create_rows
tools.description:
Add MANY rows to a Rootr (루터) DATABASE in one call. Use this instead of calling rootr_add_row in a loop — a loop leaves a half-filled table when one call fails, and burns the read quota. All-or-nothing: if any row fails validation nothing is created, and the error says which index broke. Column keys may be property NAMES or ids. Up to 500 rows per call.
Pass `upsertKey` (a column name or id) to make the call IDEMPOTENT: a row whose key already exists is UPDATED instead of duplicated, so a retried or replayed batch cannot double-load. Use it for every migration and every sync from an outside system — without it a retry after a partial failure silently creates duplicates (a real 903-row incident). The key column must be a plain stored column (text/number/date/select), not a formula, rollup or relation. Returns `created` and `updated`.

tools.name: rootr_add_column
tools.description: Add ONE column to a Rootr (루터) DATABASE. The existing columns and every row are left untouched — rows simply read empty for the new column until you fill them with rootr_update_row. type ∈ text | number | select | multi_select | status | date | checkbox | url | email | phone | person | files | relation | formula | rollup | created_time | last_edited_time | created_by | last_edited_by | unique_id ("title" is not allowed: a database already has exactly one title column). For select/multi_select/status pass options: [{ name, color, group? }] (group ∈ todo|in_progress|done, status only). For relation pass relationDatabaseId (the node id of the table it points at), and reverseName to make it TWO-WAY: the other table gets a matching column with that name, and filling either side fills the other. Use it whenever both tables need the link (calls↔applicants) — a one-way column means aggregates on the other side are silently wrong until someone backfills them by hand. For formula pass formula, e.g. "{수량} * {단가}" or "if({금액} >= 5000, \"큰 건\", \"작은 건\")" — available functions: if, concat, length, upper, lower, contains, abs, round, floor, ceil, min, max, dateBetween, now, empty. For rollup pass rollup: { relation, property?, function, where? } (function ∈ count|count_values|sum|average|min|max|show_original|percent_checked). `where` filters the LINKED rows before aggregating — [{ property, op, value? }] with op ∈ is|is_not|contains|not_contains|is_empty|is_not_empty|gt|gte|lt|lte. That is how you build "how many of this applicant's calls were no-answer": { relation: "콜", function: "count", where: [{ property: "결과", op: "is", value: "부재" }] }. A rollup may also read a FORMULA column in the linked table, and min/max work on date columns (that is how "last call date" is built). For unique_id pass prefix to get "TASK-42" style ids. For vector pass dimensions — an embedding column YOU fill with rootr_set_row_vectors and search with rootr_query_vectors (Rootr never embeds it for you; people see only "vector · N dims" in the grid). created_time / last_edited_time / created_by / last_edited_by / unique_id / formula / rollup are filled in by the server — they take no value and rootr_update_row will refuse to set them. Display options: align (left|center|right), wrap true; date columns: highlightOverdue true (past dates red — off by default), allowTime false (no time), allowRange false (no end date). Returns the created column WITH ITS id.

tools.name: rootr_update_column
tools.description:
Rename ONE column of a Rootr (루터) DATABASE, replace the choices of a select/multi_select column, edit a formula or rollup config, turn an existing relation column TWO-WAY, or exclude it from the search index (searchExcluded: true — managers only; values already indexed are removed before this returns). The column TYPE and a vector column's dimensions cannot be changed — that would rewrite every row (or every stored vector) — so passing type or dimensions is refused; add a new column and move the values instead. Call rootr_read_database first to get the exact propertyId.
RENAMES CASCADE: a new `name` also rewrites everything that refers to the column BY NAME, in the same transaction — formulas ({col} / prop("col")) in this table, button/automation {col} {col+1} {relation.col} templates here and in tables that link to this one, rollups in other tables (pinned to the column id), linked form questions (kept connected by id; the question text stays) and page live blocks (liveTable/liveStats/liveChart). Do NOT edit the formula first (a formula naming a column that does not exist yet is refused). The result has `renameCascade` {formulas, buttons, automations, rollups, forms, pages, warnings, summary}; `warnings` lists what could not follow (e.g. two form questions now landing on one column). Pass dryRun: true with `name` to get that list without changing anything.
`reverseName` on a relation column pairs it with the linked table: that table gets a matching column with this name and filling either side fills the other. Pass an empty string to unpair (neither column is deleted). Use it to make an existing one-way link two-way rather than rebuilding the table — a one-way column leaves every aggregate on the other side wrong until somebody backfills it by hand.
Display options (only what you pass changes; null resets): align left|center|right, wrap true (long text wraps), and for DATE columns highlightOverdue true (past dates in red — off by default), allowTime false (no time), allowRange false (no end date). e.g. { "allowTime": false, "allowRange": false } makes 「지원일」 a plain single date.

A relation column shows the latest 5 linked rows (contact history) and the total. Names or ids; an unknown name is refused (400), not dropped. null/[] = automatic (status, notes, dates, rollups; relations as history).

highlightOverdue.description: date only: show PAST dates in red (deadline-like columns). Default OFF — application/call dates stay plain. Refused (400) on a non-date column.

When a NEW row has the same value as an earlier row, copy the earlier row's values INTO the new row (the earlier row is untouched). { auto?: true = do it on every entry path (row add, cell, form, button/automation add_row, REST/MCP/bulk) without asking; false/omitted = only the duplicate dialog button / rootr_carry_over. label?: name of this action for the table (≤30 chars, e.g. "재등록"; toasts/merge comments use it; blank = neutral default), exclude?: [columns not copied, e.g. "접수일"], overwrite?: [columns copied even if the new row has a value; default fills empty cells only], relations?: true to copy relation columns too (default false — they are two-way), latestBy?: date column or "createdAt" — which earlier row wins when several match (latest), mark?: values stamped on the new row: { "재등록 여부": true, "구분": { map: { "A": "A(재등록)" }, else: "재등록" } } — map looks at the value the NEW row came in with; else covers any value not in map; if that column is still EMPTY when carried, the mark waits and is applied once to the first value written there later (e.g. a later button step); missing select options are added }. Names or ids. null turns it off.

The user writes the rule: { kind: "pattern", pattern: "<regex the WHOLE value must match>", flags?: "i"|"s"|"m", negate?: true (flag values that CONTAIN the pattern instead), message?: "{name}: {value} …" } — linear-time engine, no back-references/look-arounds, max 500 chars; starting points via rootr_test_value_rule { presets: true } (email, URL, intl/KR/US phone, postal codes …); formats differ per country, so pick/adapt one rather than assuming Korean formats. Other kinds: "range" (number: min/max), "date" (text reads as a date), "birthdate" (text/date; min/max = age). askDeleteRow?: true — the in-app dialog also offers deleting the row. Applies to cells, row panel, forms, REST/MCP/bulk, buttons/automations. Existing values are not changed. null turns it off.

Phone numbers compare digits only (010-1234-5678 = 01012345678); other text ignores case and spaces. Give `rowId` to check an existing row (it is excluded from the result) or `values` ({column name or id: value}) to check before adding. Each match comes with the fields the duplicate dialog shows (`preview`: status, notes, dates, rollups — or the column's dedupeShow list) and `history`: the latest 5 linked rows per relation column (e.g. call log) with the total. Only rows the caller can see are returned. Then use rootr_merge_rows, rootr_keep_duplicate or rootr_carry_over (copy the earlier row into the new one).

tools.name: rootr_set_database_buttons
tools.description:
Replace the WHOLE button list of a Rootr (루터) DATABASE (needs MANAGE). This is a full replace, not a merge — call rootr_list_database_buttons first and send back the buttons you want to KEEP, or they are dropped. Up to 12 buttons, 8 steps each.
Steps run in order and the row a step created is what the NEXT step works on, which is how "add a row → have AI write its summary → open it" becomes one press:
· {kind:"add_row", values?, database?, link?} — make a row, optionally pre-filled. Column keys may be NAMES or ids. `database` (a table id or tree path like "/01. 채용/콜 이력") puts the row in ANOTHER table — omit it for this one. `link: { relation, from: "selected"|"created" }` wires the new row to the row the person pressed on, where `relation` is the relation column IN THE TARGET table that points back here. That pair is how "press 전화 on an applicant → a call row already linked to them" becomes one press instead of switching tables and searching the person again.
  add_row also takes `match: { key: "{요청 건}", on: "업체명", normalize?: ["spaces","parens","suffix:의원","trailingDigits","case"], fill?: "empty" }` — FIND-OR-LINK instead of always creating: `key` (filled from the pressed row) is compared with the target column `on` — first exactly (spaces ignored, so "다라치과(홍대점)" picks that branch), then after `normalize` (parens drops "(긴급)"·"(소독)", suffix:X drops a trailing X, trailingDigits drops a trailing number). ONE match → no new row, the pressed row is ADDED to that row's `link` relation (fill:"empty" also fills its blank cells from `values`); NONE → created as usual; TWO OR MORE → nothing is created and the pressed row gets a "후보 여러 곳: A, B" comment so a person picks. The result says `matched: { linked, created, ambiguous }`.
· {kind:"update_rows", target:"created"|"selected", values} — set values on the rows this button just made, or on the rows the person ticked in the table.
· {kind:"ai_fill", target, propId, prompt} — let AI write ONE cell. The prompt may quote the row with {칸이름}, e.g. "{제목}과 {메모}를 한 문장으로 요약해". If the AI fails the button keeps going.
· {kind:"open_row"} — open the row this button made (UI only; over the API it just reports the id).
Values accept @today, @today+7 and @me — the server fills them in at press time, not now. A text value may also quote the pressed row with {칸이름}, e.g. "{이름} {통화 건수+1}차": computed columns (rollup, formula) are read too, {칸이름+N} / {칸이름-N} adds to a numeric value, and when several rows are selected each new row is filled from its own source row. A relation column resolves to the linked row: {지원자} is its TITLE (not the id) and {지원자.통화 건수} reads one of its columns — EXCEPT when the value is exactly "{관계 칸}" and the column it goes into is a relation to the SAME table: then the row ids are copied (e.g. 담당 매니저: "{배정 매니저}"). Ids the receiving column's relationFilter rejects are left out of that cell only (the rest still runs), commented on the row and reported in `notes`.
A button never grants permission: it runs as whoever presses it — writing into another table needs write access there too.

It runs with YOUR permissions: a button that writes a locked column stops there if you cannot edit it.

tools.name: rootr_set_database_automations
tools.description:
Replace the WHOLE automatic-rule list of a Rootr (루터) DATABASE (needs MANAGE). Full replace, not a merge — send back the rules you want to KEEP. Up to 10 rules, 8 steps each.
A rule is { label, enabled?, on, when?, schedule?, steps } and the steps are the SAME ones a button uses (add_row / update_rows / ai_fill), so there is nothing new to learn. The row that woke the rule arrives in the steps as target "selected".
· on: ["updated"] | ["created"] | ["schedule"] (one or more).
· when: { property, op, value? } — op ∈ changed_to|changed|is|is_not|contains|gt|gte|lt|lte|is_empty|is_not_empty. Prefer `changed_to` for state transitions: "is" is true on EVERY later edit too, so a rule that creates follow-up rows would create them again and again.
· schedule: { at: "09:00", days?: [1,2,3,4,5] } — required when on includes "schedule". Korean time, once a day; `when` then picks WHICH rows to act on and may use @today / @today+7 in its value.
Typical uses from the field: 투입확정 → create three follow-up-call rows at +7/+30/+90 days; 부재 3회 초과 → set the applicant to 보류; every morning at 09:00 → flag rows whose 재통화 예정일 is today.
Rules run as the person who SAVED them, never with more permission than that. A rule that a computed column (rollup/formula) triggers must use a value comparison, not changed/changed_to — the server refuses those instead of quietly never firing.
add_row `match` (find-or-link, see rootr_set_database_buttons) is how "투입확정 → 사업장 마스터에 등록" stops making duplicates for existing customers: one matching 사업장 → linked, none → created, several → a "후보 여러 곳" comment on the request row. Those notes, and relation ids skipped by a relationFilter, are written to the rule's lastError (with the row) — read them with rootr_list_database_automations.

tools.name: rootr_find_similar_rows
tools.description: Find rows in a DATABASE that are semantically similar to a given row (duplicate reports, a past answer to a similar inquiry, a similar experiment). Uses vector embeddings of the row's columns — no keyword matching. Columns marked "exclude from search index" (searchExcluded) are never indexed, and on an "own rows only" table you only get your own rows. Only rows that stand out from the rest of the table are returned (the raw cosine of unrelated rows in one table is often 0.8+, so a fixed cut-off lies): each row carries `similarityLevel` ("high" | "mid") and the raw `similarityScore`. An empty list with `compared` > 0 means "nothing is especially similar", not an error. `state`: "ready", "indexing" (the row, or `pending` other rows of the table, are not indexed yet — the rows found so far are returned; retry in a few seconds), "no-text" (the row has nothing to compare — it is empty or only its excluded columns are filled; retrying will not help) or "sync-off" (graph sync is turned off — `syncOffAt` says where to turn it back on: "node" = this table's menu, "folder" = the parent folder named in `syncOffFolder`, "workspace" = workspace settings › General).

Rows you may not edit (own-rows-only tables, manager-locked column) are refused with the reason — nothing is written if any item is invalid. To check which rows already hold a vector, read the rows (rootr_list_rows / rootr_read_database: each row has `vectors` — column id → dimensions, empty when none). tools.name: rootr_create_presentation
tools.description:
Create a new PRESENTATION node (a slide deck) in a Rootr (루터) workspace, optionally seeded with an initial theme and slides. Authoring guide: give each slide ONE assertion-style title (a claim, e.g. "Latency dropped 40% after the cache fix" — not a topic label like "Latency"), plus blocks[] (bullet-like {id, heading?, body?, icon?} items) and, where useful, a diagram ({type:"mermaid", code} — drawn on "content" slides) or images. Canvas is 16:9 (1280x720). Meaning must live in TEXT — title/blocks[].heading/blocks[].body/notes are what auto-connects into the knowledge graph; diagrams/code/html and the image pixels themselves are visual-only and are NOT indexed, so never put facts ONLY in a diagram or picture.
Images: `image` is the single primary/background image (cover, section, full-bleed); `images[]` holds additional inserted images placed on the slide. Each image is {id?, src?, alt?, placement?, prompt?, x?, y?, w?, h?}. Set `src` to an uploaded file URL (upload via POST /v1/attachments/upload, then use /api/v1/attachments/{id}/raw), an https URL, or a data: URI — you cannot upload the file bytes through these MCP tools, only reference the resulting URL. To get a REAL image, call rootr_generate_image with an English prompt (say "no text"), then put the returned `url` into the slide image's `src`; rootr_remove_image_background cuts out an image's background. Set `placement` on the primary `image`: "full" = background (full-bleed on cover/section/closing, faint on content); "right" / "top" = beside / above the blocks, content slides only; other values are ignored and a content slide without placement does not draw the image. For `images[]`, x/y/w/h give freeform PPT-style placement in 1280x720 canvas coords (drawn only when both x and y are set). ALWAYS add an `alt` caption to every image — alt text is part of the graph text spine, so a captioned image connects into the knowledge graph while an uncaptioned one does not.
Videos (Team plan and above — a Free workspace gets 403 PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED when it ADDS a video; existing ones stay editable/removable): `videos[]` (max 20 per slide) holds {id?, src, title?, poster?, x?, y?, w?, h?} in 1280x720 canvas coords (default 640x360 centred). `src` is an uploaded video file URL (upload mp4/webm ≤75MB via rootr_upload_attachment with nodeId = this deck, then use /api/v1/attachments/{id}/raw), an https video-file URL, or a YouTube/Vimeo link; `poster` is an image URL (thumbnail). `title` is a caption and joins the graph text spine. Slide `html` may instead contain <video src="…/v1/attachments/{id}/raw" controls>, <div data-video-embed="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=…">, or a YouTube/Vimeo <iframe>. Uploaded videos play through short-lived signed URLs (`vt=` query) the server adds when it returns the slide — never write `vt=` yourself; it is stripped on save.
Animations (all plans): in slide `html`, add data-anim="<effect>" to any element to animate it when the slide opens in view/present mode. Entrance effects: fade, fade-up, fade-down, fly-left, fly-right, zoom, pop, blur. Looping effects: pulse, float, spin, blink, shake. Duration/delay go in inline CSS variables, e.g. <div data-anim="fade-up" style="--anim-delay:.4s;--anim-dur:.8s">; stagger delays to set the order. Thumbnails and PDF/PPTX exports show the finished state. Your own @keyframes/animation CSS in the html also plays.
Use kind to mark each slide's role: "cover" (deck title slide), "section" (chapter divider), "content" (body slide, the default), "closing" (last slide / call to action).
Page numbers: "content" and "section" slides automatically show a page number that follows the slide order (it re-numbers itself when slides are reordered), so you do NOT set it yourself. "cover"/"closing" have none by design. The result includes `url` — the address to open this node at. Use it as-is; never guess or construct it.

tools.name: rootr_update_presentation
tools.description:
Merge-patch a Rootr (루터) PRESENTATION: update theme and/or config, or REPLACE THE WHOLE slides array (if you pass `slides`, it replaces every existing slide — call rootr_read_presentation first and resend slides you want to keep, or use rootr_append_presentation_slides / rootr_update_presentation_slide instead for incremental changes). tools.name: rootr_remember
tools.description:
Save ONE short, present-tense fact that should change how you act next time in this Rootr (루터) workspace — a team convention, a decision and its reason, a gotcha you just hit, a person's preference. Memories are SHARED WITH THE WHOLE WORKSPACE, so everyone's assistant learns it too. Keep personal notes in your own memory, not here.

THE RULE: long things go in documents, one-liners go in memory, and a memory should point at a document. Save the lesson ("captures must run in the parent window with data URIs"), not the story — write the story as a document and pass its path as `source`.

Always pass `source` when the fact came from a document: that is what lets Rootr flag the memory as "needs checking" when that document changes. A memory with no source can never notice it went stale.

Saving the same fact twice is safe — Rootr replaces it instead of piling up duplicates.

EDITING: pass `memoryId` (the `id` from rootr_recall) to fix that exact memory in place — omit it to save a new one. Editing marks the memory 유효 again (a person or their assistant just re-confirmed it).

kind.description: What kind of fact. Korean values are canonical and what gets stored; the English aliases in parentheses are accepted and normalized. 지시 (instruction) = how the team wants work done, 사람 (person) = someone's role/preference, 프로젝트 (project) = ongoing work or constraints, 참고 (reference) = a pointer to an external resource

This is NOT a copy: each address gets access to the ORIGINAL node (and everything under it, if it is a folder) at `access` = read (view, default) | comment | write (edit). They always see the latest version; with write their edits land in the original. People with a Rootr account on that (verified) email open it from their inbox (rootr_list_doc_mail) with that access, even if they are not members of your workspace — they never see your workspace tree, members or search. Needs WRITE on the node as a workspace member (the same bar as sharing); you can give at most your own level, never manage. The result lists each recipient with `emailed` (false = the email failed; the access still stands). instructions:
Rootr (pronounced "루터" in Korean — when the user says 루터, they mean Rootr) is the team's cloud document workspace. Use these tools whenever the user asks to read, write, append to, edit, or search their Rootr/루터 documents. Prefer rootr_append for adding content and rootr_edit for targeted changes; use rootr_write only for full rewrites. Beyond documents, this server also covers workspace scaffolding (planning/creating/applying document trees), typed LOG datastores (structured entries + stats), GraphRAG root-cause Q&A (rootr_ask), GitHub-style issue trackers, DATABASE rows (read schema + rows, add/update/delete rows — e.g. move a kanban card by changing its status column, via rootr_read_database / rootr_add_row / rootr_update_row / rootr_delete_row), CRM nodes (companies/contacts/deals/activities/tasks via the rootr_crm_* tools), and webhooks. To put a screenshot or photo into a document, use rootr_attach_image_to_document (upload + insert in one step) or rootr_upload_attachment (upload only, returns a URL/markdown to place yourself).

Node types — pick the block that fits, never fake everything with markdown files: DOCUMENT = free-form markdown narrative (overviews, specs, decision logs); DATABASE = typed columns + views (table/board/calendar/timeline) for anything trackable — tasks, requirements, risks, milestones; SPREADSHEET = grid with formulas when content needs calculation (budgets, models, estimates) — author with the rootr_*_spreadsheet / rootr_*_sheet tools (create/read/update, per-sheet create/update/delete, rootr_patch_spreadsheet_cells for cell values/formulas); WHITEBOARD = freeform visual canvas (flow diagrams, brainstorming, journey maps) — author with the rootr_*_whiteboard tools (create/read/update the shapes[]/edges[] scene); FORM = fillable intake from people outside the tree, optionally feeding a DATABASE (surveys, request queues) — author with the rootr_*_form tools (create/read/update fields, rootr_list_form_responses / rootr_submit_form_response for responses, rootr_*_form_share_link for public links); ISSUE_TRACKER = GitHub-style issues with #numbers, states, labels, comments (bug/work tracking with a lifecycle); CRM = full sales CRM: companies, contacts with lifecycle stages & auto lead-scoring, multi-pipeline deals (kanban), an activity timeline, follow-up tasks, and CSV import/export — use for sales/lead/customer tracking; never fake a CRM with plain DATABASEs (use the rootr_crm_* tools: rootr_crm_create/get/update, rootr_crm_list_companies/upsert_company/get_company, rootr_crm_list_contacts/upsert_contact/get_contact, rootr_crm_list_deals/upsert_deal/get_deal/move_deal, rootr_crm_log_activity/list_activities, rootr_crm_upsert_task/list_tasks, rootr_crm_import); PRESENTATION = slide deck (16:9 HTML slides with themes) — author via the rootr_*_presentation tools (rootr_create_presentation, rootr_read_presentation, rootr_update_presentation, rootr_append_presentation_slides, rootr_update_presentation_slide, rootr_reorder_presentation_slides, plus rootr_generate_image / rootr_remove_image_background for slide art), never as markdown documents; ALWAYS rootr_read_presentation before updating so slide ids line up; RECORDING = audio recording with a diarized (speaker-labeled) transcript and minutes — fully drivable from MCP: rootr_create_recording → rootr_upload_recording_audio (upload a local audio file; stores it as status UPLOADED, does NOT transcribe) → rootr_transcribe_recording (explicit step that runs speech-to-text and spends AI credits) → poll rootr_read_recording until status READY → read the transcript, rename speakers with rootr_rename_recording_speakers, and write the minutes yourself with rootr_write (preferred — no AI credits) or call rootr_summarize_recording for Rootr's built-in summary document; SIGNED = 서명문서 · 전자결재 · 국가R&D 전자연구노트 — a markdown document that FREEZES on submit, collects ordered Ed25519 signatures with RFC 3161 timestamps, and is hash-chained into a workspace ledger so tampering is provable; cannot be deleted (30-year retention). Use it whenever the content must be provable — 결재/승인 문서, 연구노트, 점검 기록 — via rootr_create_signed_document, rootr_read_signed_document, rootr_set_approval_line, rootr_apply_research_note_preset, rootr_submit_signed_document, rootr_sign_document, rootr_reject_signed_document, rootr_revise_signed_document, rootr_list_signed_documents, rootr_bulk_sign_documents, rootr_verify_signed_document, rootr_verify_ledger. NEVER invent a signing code: always rootr_request_signing_code first and ASK THE HUMAN for the 6 digits that arrive in their mail — that code is the only evidence a person (not an agent) pressed sign; FOLDER = grouping; LOG store = typed event table whose relation fields auto-build a lineage graph (metrics, incidents, pipeline events — use the rootr_*_log_* tools).

Sending a document to someone by email (문서 보내기 · 문서함): rootr_send_document gives 1-20 email addresses access to the ORIGINAL node (not a copy) at access read|comment|write — they see live edits, and with write their edits land in the original; an account on that email opens it from its inbox, others read it via the email link after typing their address; rootr_list_doc_mail (box inbox|sent) / rootr_read_doc_mail / rootr_set_doc_mail_access / rootr_revoke_doc_mail cover the mailbox. Only send to addresses the user gave you. When any tool result ends with "📬 New documents received", tell the user right away (title and sender) and offer to open them with rootr_read_doc_mail. rootr_add_doc_mail_webhook makes Rootr POST doc_mail.received / revoked / read to the user's own URL (for their automations).

Scaffolding discipline — treat "set up a workspace for X" exactly like "build me this app": you ask a few clarifying questions, write it, compile it, run the tests, leave a README, and report. The user should only have to type that one sentence; everything else finishes inside the conversation. Never ask and then stop. The loop is plan → ask → design → review → fix → apply → manual → test, and skipping a step is how a workspace ends up as a pile of thin markdown files: (1) rootr_scaffold_plan on the raw intent — it hands back the METHOD, never a template or a domain skeleton (there are none, deliberately): analyzeFirst, designRules, buildingBlocks, questionPolicy, loop; (2) work out how the job ACTUALLY runs using the `analyzeFirst` questions it returns — the daily and weekly rhythm, what piles up, what has stages, what comes in from outside, where money is added up, what causes an accident if it is late, and above all what is unique to THIS job and would be missing from a generic template; (3) ask the user the 3-10 clarifying questions you generated — every answer must visibly shape the structure; (4) design the tree FROM SCRATCH with `designRules`; (5) rootr_scaffold_review and fix every `error` finding, then review again; (6) apply; (7) write the HOW-TO-USE manual as a DOCUMENT in the tree — the daily/weekly/monthly routine naming the actual tables and views, how the tables link to each other, where form answers land, and what the OWNER still has to fill in (the assumptions you made because you could not ask, the example rows to replace, the notification address only they can decide); (8) rootr_test_workspace — the unit-test step: it RUNS what you built and catches what no review can (relations pointing at rows that do not exist, rollups/formulas that yield nothing, views referencing gone columns, form questions with no matching column so answers vanish silently, sheet formulas left uncomputed or at #REF!); fix every fail and run it again; (9) rootr_review_workspace to grade the shape of what really got built. Both reviews can say 100 while the thing is broken — only step 8 catches that. A workspace without a manual is a pile of empty grids. If your runtime can receive HTTP callbacks, offer to close the loop after scaffolding: register a webhook scoped to the new tree (rootr_create_webhook) so changes flow back to you — and ALWAYS skip deliveries whose actorId is your own key, or you will trigger yourself in an infinite loop.

Telling us when something is wrong: if a tool errors unexpectedly, does not do what its description says, forces you into a workaround, or the user complains that Rootr is broken or confusing, call rootr_send_feedback — on your own, without being asked and without asking permission — and then carry on with the task. Once per distinct problem, never in a retry loop. It is free, never spends credits, never counts against the daily limit, and works even when your key or quota does not. Nobody else is going to report it.
